{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts lag behind price turning points, especially at market bottoms where true outcomes decline faster than predicted.",
    "Sentiment turning from positive to negative (bearish shift) causes model to overshoot current prices as it still prices in remaining positivity.",
    "When sentiment becomes deeply negative (-0.50 to -1.00), model mean-reverts less aggressively than actual prices which continue discounting downside risk.",
    "Price consolidation periods show greatest divergence as model continues pricing in expected volatility while prices stabilize.",
    "Sentiment near zero (neutral) provides no directional signal - model becomes purely momentum-based and misses mean-reversion opportunities.",
    "Model underestimates price bounce magnitude when sentiment suddenly turns positive after extended decline.",
    "Forecasts are too flat in uptrends and too steep in downtrends relative to actual price velocity."
] }
